ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against Canada's Criminal Code provisions on proceeds of crime, the United Nations Act, S.C. 1985, c. U-2, and the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, as administered by the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Canadian Security Intelligence Service, and additionally against OFAC SDN and UN Security Council consolidated lists where cross-border payment rails include U.S.-dollar clearing. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person (PEP) as defined under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. FINTRAC reporting entity requirements apply to the partnership's designated money service business or reporting entity activities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (online portal operated by ServiceOntario)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name may be in English or French. Names in a non-Latin script must be transliterated into English or French and filed in that form. The legal name must include the expression 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP' or 'L.P.' or equivalent in the recognized statutory form. A separate trade name may be registered under the Business Names Act and must comply with the same distinctiveness requirements.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected by the Ontario Business Registry, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Director appointed under the Business Names Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.17, within 30 days of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds of distinctiveness and a proposed NUANS search result. The Director will issue a reconsideration decision in writing. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may submit a revised name through the same online registry interface without losing the underlying registration appointment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. Ontario accepts a virtual commercial registered office address provided that it is a physically locatable street address in Ontario, is not a post office box, and is maintained by the registered office provider to accept service of process during normal business hours. For this digital media buying affiliate line of business, a virtual office is acceptable provided the partnership retains a registered office address in Ontario and complies with the record-keeping requirements of the Limited Partnerships Act.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate, quantified at approximately 8% per year for a non-licensed, non-consumer-facing media arbitrage partnership. The probability of an unannounced physical inspection rises above 20% if FINTRAC receives a suspicious transaction report or if CRA initiates an audit that includes the general partner.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, ss. 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 15 (Ontario); Limited Partnerships Regulations O. Reg 54/96; Extra-Provincial Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.27 (if corporate general partner); Business Names Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.17 (for any assumed name)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Business Registry (ora.on.ca), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Government of Ontario
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form prescribed under s.4(1) of the Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for an Ontario limited partnership. The Declaration must state each limited partner's agreed contribution, but no minimum contribution is prescribed. A corporate general partner must be in good standing under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario) or, if extra-provincially incorporated, licensed under the Extra-Provincial Corporations Act before acting as general partner in Ontario.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: the General Partner accepts the subscription of the initial Limited Partner in an Ontario limited partnership named per the approved NUANS report. RESOLVED FURTHER: the registered office of the Partnership shall be [address], Toronto, Ontario. RESOLVED FURTHER: the officers of the General Partner, jointly and severally, are authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Ontario Business Registry, obtain the CRA Business Number and applicable GST/HST and payroll accounts, engage counsel and a registered agent, open bank accounts, and take all ancillary actions, such authority continuing until revoked by written resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search Report and Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (online at ora.on.ca) through an accredited NUANS search house
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed partnership names for a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) preliminary report. The proposed name must include the phrase 'Limited Partnership','L.P.' or 'societe en commandite' and must not be confusingly similar to any existing corporate or partnership name in Ontario. The NUANS report is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance and must accompany the Declaration.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS search request form
List of up to three proposed partnership names
Representation letter from the formation agent or legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or deemed too similar, select the next available name from the same NUANS report and resubmit; no refund of the search fee is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry; execution witnessed or notarized in accordance with Ontario law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Declaration of Limited Partnership under s.4(1) of the Limited Partnerships Act. State the full partnership name, registered office address, mailing address, principal place of business, nature of business (digital advertising media arbitrage and affiliate lead generation, ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810), full legal name and address of each general partner and each limited partner, the amount of each limited partner's agreed contribution, the term if limited, and any other prescribed particulars. The Declaration must be executed by every general partner (and by a limited partner only if so provided) before a witness or notary public.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Limited Partnership in the prescribed form
Valid NUANS name search report
Certified copy of the corporate general partner's certificate of incorporation or corporate records
Extra-provincial license or evidence of good standing for a non-Ontario corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry notifies of a deficiency, re-execute an amended Declaration and refile; deficiencies are cured by resubmission of the corrected form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration with Ontario Business Registry and Pay Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (online portal ora.on.ca), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the fully executed Declaration of Limited Partnership through the Ontario Business Registry online system. Pay the prescribed filing fee of CAD 60.00 (approximately USD 45.00). The Registry will issue a filed acknowledgment and a stamped electronic copy. The limited partnership comes into legal existence upon the date of filing as endorsed by the Registry, per s.9 of the Limited Partnerships Act.
required_dossiers: Executed Declaration of Limited Partnership
NUANS name search report
Counsel's closing certificate or solicitor's transmittal letter
Proof of payment (credit card or registry account debit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, correct the stated deficiency on the Declaration, obtain fresh execution by the general partners, and refile with the Registry; any additional filing fee must be paid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration (EPC Compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership's Business Number (BN) with the CRA and open the applicable program accounts: GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 per annum, payroll (RC1) for employee remuneration, and corporate income tax references for the general partner. The limited partnership is fiscally transparent: income flows through to partners, and the partnership must file an annual partnership information return (T5013) if it has a non-resident member, carries on business in Canada, or has more than two partners. Keep a completed T5013 Summary and partner allocation schedules on file.
required_dossiers: Filed Declaration of Limited Partnership (stamped copy)
General partner's legal name, address and identification (BN or SIN)
Completed RC1 and GST/HST registration forms
Authorization of authorized representatives (Form T183 or RP-1 if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects the registration due to a name, address or ID mismatch, correct the data through CRA My Business Account and resubmit; penalties are generally waived if corrected within 30 days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Registered Office Maintenance and Post-Formation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian financial institution (Schedule I bank or credit union); Ontario Business Registry for amendments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the filed Declaration, the general partner resolution and the partnership agreement to open a business bank account (or a US-dollar account/arrangement supporting Mercury-ACH, wire transfer or Wise rails). Maintain a physical registered office in Ontario and promptly file an amended Declaration with the Ontario Business Registry upon any change in registered office, general partner, or partnership name. Monitor the federal and provincial beneficial ownership registry obligations, including any filing requirements imposed under Ontario's Beneficial Ownership Information Act, 2023 once in force, and maintain internal AML/KYC dossiers reflecting the medium-risk enhanced profile of performance media buying.
required_dossiers: Filed Declaration of Limited Partnership (stamped copy)
General partner resolution authorizing banking arrangements
Limited partnership agreement and contribution schedule
AML/KYC beneficial ownership documentation
T5013 partnership information return template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution delays account opening pending KYC, supply an updated partnership agreement, a certificate of good standing from the Registry, and a legal opinion on the authority of signing officers; escalate to the bank's commercial compliance group.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal tax administration, Business Number (BN) registration, and GST/HST program-account (RT) administration; primary portal: CRA My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-individuals/business-account.html) and Business Registration Online. Ontario Ministry of Finance — provincial tax administration for Ontario-source filings (including the Ontario partnership information return and Employer Health Tax); portal: ontario.ca/page/taxes-rebates-credits. The 8% Ontario provincial component of HST is collected and administered by the CRA; no separate Ontario indirect-tax registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign person establishing or acquiring an interest in an Ontario limited partnership engaged in performance media buying, the statutory sequence is: (i) register the LP on the Ontario Business Registry under the Limited Partnerships Act (R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16) and appoint a general partner located or served in Ontario; (ii) apply to the CRA for the LP's 9-digit Business Number (BN) and RT (GST/HST) program account, using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) or the CRA Business Registration Online service, designating the Ontario head office and a representative partner for service; (iii) if the value of the LP's worldwide taxable supplies, including those of associates, exceeds CAD 30,000 in the current or any preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, GST/HST registration and remittance is mandatory from the day the threshold is exceeded; where the LP makes only zero-rated Canadian supplies (e.g., qualifying offshore media-buying services to non-residents), the LP may nonetheless elect to register voluntarily to claim input tax credits; (iv) file the applicable Ontario partnership information return with the Ontario Ministry of Finance and, where the LP has Ontario-resident or non-resident partners allocated Ontario-source income, remit Ontario provincial tax through the respective partners' returns. The BN serves as the consolidated federal tax identifier (the 'TIN'); no separate federal VAT-ID certificate is issued outside the CRA program-account confirmation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — an Ontario limited partnership is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Income Tax Act (Ontario): the partnership computes income, deductions, and credits at the partnership level, but no entity-level federal or Ontario income tax is imposed; each partner (resident or non-resident) is taxed on its allocable share of Canadian-source and Ontario-source income. For GST/HST purposes the LP itself is a 'person' under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act and registers, collects, and remits HST in its own BN program account; the LP is accordingly the reporting registrant for indirect tax, while the partners bear the direct income tax. Non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP are subject to Part I tax under the Income Tax Act on their partnership share and must file Canadian tax returns; limited partners are further constrained by the at-risk amount and limited-recourse rules (ss. 96(2.1) and 96(2.2) ITA) restricting loss allocation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing capital controls, mandatory export-receipt surrender, or general restrictions on conversion or repatriation. The Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers applicable anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing obligations for reporting entities, while the Canada Revenue Agency administers tax reporting and transfer-pricing rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial and investment transactions. Current-account receipts, including advertising, affiliate commissions, and other service income, may generally be converted and remitted without a statutory conversion deadline or mandatory surrender ratio. Capital-account transactions are also generally permitted, subject to corporate-law authority, lender or investor restrictions, sanctions, beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds review, withholding-tax obligations, partnership allocation rules, transfer-pricing requirements, and accurate tax reporting. An Ontario limited partnership should document capital contributions, partner loans, distributions, intercompany charges, and related-party settlements. Canadian non-resident withholding tax may apply to specified payments, including certain interest, royalties, management fees, and other amounts deemed to arise in Canada; the applicable treaty position and statutory rate must be confirmed before payment. A limited partnership is generally fiscally transparent for Canadian income-tax purposes, but classification, filing, withholding, and reporting consequences depend on the partnership agreement, partner status, income character, and applicable federal and provincial rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general requirement to repatriate or convert foreign-currency receipts within a prescribed period. Foreign-currency export and service receipts may remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at commercially agreed rates. The partnership should retain contracts, invoices, delivery or performance evidence, payment records, bank statements, and accounting support establishing the commercial purpose and tax treatment. Large international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, including aggregated transfers within the applicable 24-hour period, may trigger reporting by the financial institution or money-services business to FINTRAC. Cross-border tax reporting, related-party documentation, GST/HST treatment, and foreign-asset reporting may apply independently of any FX conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary collections, payments, and foreign-currency management; low as the sole treasury bank. Wise Business availability and features for Canadian partnerships must be confirmed at onboarding and do not eliminate Canadian AML, tax, sanctions, recordkeeping, or beneficial-ownership obligations. Mercury is principally designed for eligible United States businesses and should not be assumed to onboard an Ontario limited partnership without an eligible United States structure and verified business nexus. Offshore digital EMIs cannot provide unrestricted Canadian deposit-taking or domestic payment services unless appropriately authorized or operating through a permitted partner. Client-money segregation, safeguarding, withdrawal, account-freeze, correspondent-bank, and jurisdictional-access risks require a domestic-bank fallback. Affiliate media buying may receive enhanced review because of high transaction velocity, digital advertising intermediaries, chargebacks, lead-quality disputes, platform dependence, and potentially opaque beneficial flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal Canadian statutory requirement that all directors or partners appear physically for account opening. A Canadian bank may permit remote onboarding, but policy varies by institution, entity type, ownership structure, residence of controlling persons, business complexity, and risk rating. An Ontario limited partnership normally must provide the partnership agreement, provincial registration evidence, general-partner authority, beneficial-ownership information, tax identifiers, business address, expected activity, and identity verification for general partners, limited partners meeting ownership or control thresholds, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners. A branch or video interview may be required, particularly where the controlling persons are non-resident, the partnership is newly formed, the business is digital, or expected cross-border flows are material. A limited partnership should identify the general partner with authority to bind the partnership; banks may require incorporation and ownership documents for a corporate general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear control structure, nominee partners, incomplete limited-partner register, or failure to identify the general partner and ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership agreement and amendments; Ontario registration record; partner register and ownership chart to natural persons; corporate records for any corporate general partner; resolutions appointing authorized signatories; government identification and address evidence; beneficial-ownership certification; explanation of control rights and distribution rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident owners or directors, remote-only onboarding, residential or virtual office address, or no credible Canadian operating footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or serviced-office agreement where applicable; Canadian business-number and provincial registrations; tax correspondence; management and staffing evidence; customer and supplier contracts; website and platform profiles; business-plan memorandum; explanation of Canadian nexus, decision-making, and expected banking activity; source-of-wealth evidence for controlling persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Affiliate media buying, lead generation, advertising arbitrage, high transaction velocity, multiple payment processors, or platform settlements inconsistent with the stated business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed funds-flow diagram; platform and advertiser agreements; insertion orders; affiliate-network agreements; sample invoices; campaign and lead-validation methodology; refund and chargeback policy; expected monthly volume, counterparties, countries, currencies, average ticket, and transaction purpose; reconciliation procedures; evidence of platform account ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital, partner loans, or related-party transfers lacking a clear legal and economic purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed contribution or loan agreement; partner resolutions; capitalization table; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; originating-bank statements; accounting entries; repayment or distribution terms; related-party disclosure; tax analysis; wire instructions matching the legal documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned or restricted parties, privacy-enhancing intermediaries, cryptocurrency exposure, or unexplained third-party settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty master file; sanctions and adverse-media screening records; beneficial-ownership evidence; contractual purpose; invoice and delivery evidence; payment-chain explanation; compliance policy; transaction-monitoring controls; prohibition or approval matrix for virtual-asset and third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity materially exceeds the initial profile or includes frequent international wires with generic payment descriptions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board or partner-approved banking profile; 12-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-volume assumptions; currency and corridor schedule; standardized payment-purpose taxonomy; monthly reconciliation; management accounts; explanations for seasonality and variance; prompt profile-update protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax, registration, or reporting inconsistencies, including missing business number, GST/HST uncertainty, foreign reporting gaps, or mismatch between partnership classification and bank representations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA business-number confirmation; applicable GST/HST registration or exemption analysis; federal and Ontario filings; partnership information returns where applicable; tax-residency certifications; accounting memorandum on partnership classification; transfer-pricing policy; professional tax-adviser confirmation where complexity warrants.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital contributions through an account held in the legal name of the Ontario limited partnership, preferably from an account held by the documented contributing partner or its fully disclosed parent. Use the bank's prescribed wire instructions, exact legal name, account number, transit and institution identifiers, SWIFT/BIC where applicable, and a payment reference such as "partner capital contribution" or "partner loan under agreement dated [date]." Do not mix capital, revenue, customer funds, and partner loans without ledger-level segregation. Maintain the contribution or loan agreement, partner approval, source-of-funds evidence, originating-bank confirmation, and accounting entry. For USD receipts, use a Canadian USD account or an approved correspondent route and document the FX rate, fees, and settlement date. Confirm sanctions screening, intermediary-bank requirements, incoming-wire fees, tax characterization, and any non-resident withholding implications before remittance. Canadian banks and reporting entities may collect identity, purpose, source-of-funds, and beneficial-ownership information and may file applicable FINTRAC reports.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian domestic electronic transfers or wires for Canadian suppliers and SWIFT cross-border wires for foreign advertising platforms, vendors, and service providers. A SWIFT MT103 is a payment message and not an independent legal settlement instrument; retain the bank confirmation, end-to-end transaction reference, invoice, contract, beneficiary verification, and proof of performance. Use commercial letters of credit only where counterparty, jurisdiction, shipment, or documentary risk justifies the cost; the issuing bank will require credit support, KYC, sanctions screening, and compliant documents under the applicable letter-of-credit rules. For digital advertising settlements, establish approved beneficiary master data, dual authorization, callback verification for changes, invoice-to-contract matching, campaign or platform evidence, sanctions screening, and reconciliation to platform statements. Confirm whether the payment is a service fee, commission, royalty, reimbursement, or partner distribution because characterization can affect withholding tax, GST/HST, transfer pricing, and financial reporting. Avoid third-party settlement unless contractually justified, pre-approved, and documented.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with an authorized Canadian bank or other appropriately regulated counterparty, used to hedge documented forecast or committed foreign-currency receipts and payments; maintain hedge designation, notional, tenor, counterparty, exposure evidence, and valuation records.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency or jurisdiction is not freely deliverable, subject to counterparty eligibility, documentation, settlement mechanics, sanctions controls, and confirmation that the transaction is a genuine commercial hedge rather than speculative dealing.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for recurring or material multi-currency funding exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral and netting terms, counterparty credit limits, valuation controls, and accounting treatment.

FX spot transactions for ordinary conversion of operating receipts and payments; use centralized dealing authority, competitive pricing evidence, and reconciliation of trade confirmations to bank statements.

FX options or collars may be considered for material exposures where the partnership understands premium, liquidity, early-termination, collateral, and mark-to-market risks; obtain legal, treasury, and accounting approval before execution.

Do not represent customer funds or unhedged speculative positions as operating treasury activity. Review derivatives reporting, clearing, trade-repository, margin, and documentation requirements with the executing Canadian financial institution because obligations depend on counterparty status, product, notional thresholds, and transaction type.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Limited Partnership Declaration—Renewal and Maintenance of Current Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ServiceOntario—Ontario Business Registry (Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal filed on or before the 5th anniversary of the most recent registration date; any change to general partner list, limited partner capital contributions, or registered head office must be declared within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If registration lapses, the limited partners cease to enjoy the statutory limited-liability shield; fines up to CAD 2,000 for false declarations per offence, and inability to maintain a court action in Ontario until the registration is revived.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return, including Schedule 50 and Limited Partner allocation schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 5 months after the LP's fiscal period end; by June 30 following a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under Income Tax Act s. 162(1): CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; for partnerships with 501+ members, s. 162(7) penalty of CAD 1,000 per day, minimum CAD 1,000, maximum CAD 50,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return (GST34) for a registrant with an annual filing election in place
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the LP's fiscal year end; March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty equal to 5% of net tax owing plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; late-payment interest at the CRA prescribed rate (approximately 8% in 2025) compounded daily; mandatory e-filing applies to registrants above CAD 1,000,000 in annual revenue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Summary and T4 slips for LP employees, with annual Canada Pension Plan / Employment Insurance reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T4 Summary and slips due on or before the last day of February following the calendar year of remuneration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act s. 162(1) of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per information return, plus late-instalment interest if payroll remittances were underpaid during the year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No Ontario statutory audit is imposed on a private limited partnership by the Limited Partnerships Act unless the LP agreement so requires; an annual independent audit becomes compulsory when the LP is a reporting issuer, operates as an investment fund under NI 81-106, or files an offering memorandum relying on the prospectus exemption where investors demand audited statements. For a digital media-buying affiliate operation with no public securities offering, the audit obligation is contractual rather than statutory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook (IFRS) applies if the LP is a reporting issuer or where the partnership agreement or investors mandate IFRS; otherwise Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE—Part II) is the default framework for a private Ontario LP. Performance-based affiliate commissions and media arbitrage revenue should be recognized on an accrual basis consistently with the go-forward partnership fiscal period.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario's Limited Partnerships Act does not require public disclosure of limited partner identities; the annual confirmatory step requires the general partner to verify the Schedule 50 allocations and the contribution table against the T5013 issued to each limited partner, and to deliver an amended declaration within 30 days if any limited partner's capital contribution changes. Canada's federal beneficial-ownership registry under Bill C-42 applies to CBCA corporations only, not to Ontario LPs, so UBO vigilance is a risk-measure for funder/adtech counterparties rather than a government filing; prudent practice is an annual internal confirmation of all limited partners at each T5013 issuance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners with capital contribution schedules and allocation percentages
Register of General Partners with management authority records
Minute Book containing general partner resolutions and consents
Registered office records including the Ontario LP Declaration and any amendments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 450 per year for Ontario registered office and registered agent services, including the 5-year declaration renewal preparation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 12,000 per full annual audit for a small-to-mid-sized private media-buying partnership if contractually triggered; USD 1,500 – 4,500 for a review engagement under ASPE if the LP agreement only requires a review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% + Ontario 11.5% for general corporate income; note: LP is pass-through, partners taxed at their own rates)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction (federal 9% + Ontario 10.2% on first CAD 500,000 active business income), SR&ED tax credits, Ontario Innovation Tax Credit, and other provincial incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T5013 (Partnership Information Return), filed via CRA My Business Account or authorized tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the last day of the fifth month after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name and mailing address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full legal name and address of the partnership; if non-resident partners exist, ensure address is current for correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business Number (BN) and program account (e.g., RC0001)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The BN is issued by CRA; non-resident partners must be identified with their own tax identification numbers.
Use the partnership's fiscal year-end; for non-resident partners, this determines the reporting period for their share of income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income (loss) to each partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income based on partnership agreement; non-resident partners must report their share in their home jurisdiction and may claim treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident partner information (name, address, country of residence, and share of income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide complete details for each non-resident partner; this triggers Part XIII withholding obligations on distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500; additional penalty of CAD 100 per partner per day (max CAD 2,500) for failure to provide required information.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII withholding tax on distributions to non-resident partners; for partnerships, withholding applies to the partner's share of Canadian-source income, not merely distributions)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partner must submit Form NR301 (Certificate of Residency) to the partnership; the partnership then applies the reduced treaty rate. For US partners, the Canada-US treaty reduces withholding to 15% on dividends, but for partnership income, it may be exempt if no permanent establishment exists in Canada.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 10% (e.g., US, UK); Interest: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 15% (e.g., US) or 0% for arm's length interest under certain treaties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 50 million gross revenue or CAD 10 million in cross-border transactions with non-arm's length parties
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply. Partnerships must demonstrate real economic activity, including substantive operations, employees, and decision-making in Canada, to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful evasion of tax by underreporting income, claiming false deductions, or failing to file returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fine up to 200% of tax evaded, maximum CAD 200,000, and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they fail to withhold and remit; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a partnership without economic substance to artificially shift profits or avoid Canadian tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, penalties up to 50% of tax avoided, and potential criminal charges for tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the tax avoided and penalties; may face civil restitution and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), e.g., not reporting large cash transactions or suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2 million for corporations, and imprisonment for individuals up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for fines and imprisonment if they knowingly fail to implement AML compliance; travel bans and asset freezes may apply.
